name: mist_api_call
description: Call the Juniper Mist REST API. Host is selected from the saved region; a static API token is attached automatically; all paths are under /api/v1. Blast radius: GET=low, POST/PUT/PATCH=medium, DELETE=destructive (metadata only, never blocks).

function.name: mist_api_call
function.description:
Call the Juniper Mist REST API. ONE tool; host + auth resolved automatically. Supply only method + path (+ body/query). Returns {status_code,data,error,blast_radius}; check status_code < 400.

Juniper Mist is a CLOUD-MANAGED network platform (Wireless / Wired / WAN Assurance + Marvis). Everything is scoped under an ORG and its SITES; all endpoints share the /api/v1 prefix.

URL SHAPE: /api/v1/<scope>/<scope_id>/<object>[/<object_id>]  (scope ∈ self|orgs|sites|msp)

START HERE (always resolve real ids first — never guess org_id/site_id):
  GET /api/v1/self                          Who am I: privileges + org_ids this token can see
  GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}                 Org detail
  GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/sites           List sites (site_id lives here)
  GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}               Site detail

INVENTORY & DEVICES (device TYPE enum is EXACTLY ap|gateway|switch — there is NO "all"; OMIT type to get every type):
  GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/inventory       Org device inventory (claimed serials + MACs). To see switches pass query_params {"type":"switch"} (comma-sep OK, e.g. "switch,gateway"); OMIT type for ALL types. Do NOT pass "all" — invalid enum. Inventory lists CLAIMED devices REGARDLESS of connection state — a DISCONNECTED switch STILL appears here.
  GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/inventory/search  query_params {"type":"switch","status":"disconnected"} — status enum connected|disconnected; the way to answer "which switches are down".
  GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/inventory/count   query_params {"distinct":"status"} for an up/down rollup.
  GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/devices       Config of devices assigned to a site (type-filterable {"type":"switch"}; NO "all").
  GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/stats/devices LIVE device status/uptime/version. DEFAULTS to type=ap — for switches pass {"type":"switch"}. status enum all|connected|disconnected (default all). Rows carry live "status"/"uptime"/"last_seen".
  GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/stats/devices/{device_id}  One device's live stats

CLIENTS & INSIGHTS:
  GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/stats/clients Connected wireless clients
  GET /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/insights/...  Assurance insights / SLE metrics

CONFIG (writes hit the live cloud):
  GET  /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/wlans        List WLANs
  GET  /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/wlans/{wlan_id}  One WLAN
  POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/wlans        Create a WLAN (medium)
  GET  /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/wlans          Org-level WLAN templates

PAGINATION (SILENT — #1 cause of "missing" devices/clients): list/search endpoints DEFAULT to limit=100, page=1 and do NOT announce more. If a result has exactly your limit of rows, ASSUME there is more — raise {"limit":1000} or page through ({"page":2}...) until a page returns fewer than the limit. Never conclude "there are only N" off one default page.

NOTES: ALWAYS GET /api/v1/self first for org_id, then /orgs/{org_id}/sites for site_id — never invent ids. To answer "show me the switches / are any down" query INVENTORY with {"type":"switch"} (includes disconnected) — do NOT rely on site stats/devices alone (APs by default). Rate limit 5,000/hour per token. A 401 = wrong/expired token (Settings -> Juniper Mist). A 404 = wrong path or bad id — re-resolve ids, do not brute-force names. An empty [] with status 200 is a valid empty result, not a failure.

query_params.description: URL query parameters as key-value pairs (optional, e.g. {"limit": 100})
